<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We present a new determination of the primordial helium abundance based on new, high-quality Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) observations of 54 metal-poor H
                    <jats:sc>ii</jats:sc>
                    regions. These regions have been observed and analyzed uniformly. We also describe a number of updates to our methodology, including updated helium emissivities. Enabled by the large, high-quality dataset, we examine our sample targets for potential systematic errors, which could bias their results. We perform a standard 95% confidence level (CL)
                    <jats:italic>χ</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    cut and find that a significantly larger fraction (47/54 = 87%) of our sample qualifies than for previous datasets. We also screen for quality and reliability, flagging targets that may introduce significant systematic errors, producing a dataset of 41 targets. In a significant breakthrough for the field, that dataset includes 15 high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) targets with low metallicity (O/H ≤ 4 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−5</jats:sup>
                    ). Due to this low-metallicity dataset, for the first time, a weighted average for determining the primordial helium abundance (
                    <jats:italic>y</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>p</jats:sub>
                    ) is well justified and produces a robust result. By weighted average of our 15 low-metallicity targets, we determine
                    <jats:italic>y</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>p</jats:sub>
                     = 0.08146 ± 0.00058, with the corresponding mass fraction
                    <jats:italic>Y</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>p</jats:sub>
                     = 0.2458 ± 0.0013. This result achieves an unprecedented precision of 0.5%, and it is in good agreement with the Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) result,
                    <jats:italic>Y</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>p</jats:sub>
                     = 0.2467 ± 0.0002, based on the Planck determination of the baryon density.
                  </jats:p>
title:
The LBT Y
                    <sub>p</sub>
                    Project. IV. A New Value of the Primordial Helium Abundance
